headline: Default pair risks are moderate: shared file-based workflows can leak or cascade errors, while prompt-injection and compliance risks are limited by Perplexity’s vendor-hosted isolation and AutoGPT’s lack of direct browser use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, and Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context. There is no documented shared channel or direct output bridge, so prompt injection is not default-dangerous; it mainly requires manual transfer or file handoff.
conditions: IF the operator copies Perplexity output into AutoGPT prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared folder or manual paste workflow, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep a human review step before copying text between agents.
Use separate folders for each agent's inputs and outputs.
Strip instructions from Perplexity outputs before feeding AutoGPT.
Disable any auto-import of downloaded files into AutoGPT.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context on vendor infrastructure. If sensitive files are moved from AutoGPT into Perplexity, data can leave the host; the pair lacks a built-in isolation boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF the operator uploads AutoGPT-generated files or secrets into Perplexity, those contents may be transmitted to vendor systems.
IF AutoGPT writes sensitive artifacts into a shared directory that Perplexity users then upload, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Do not upload secrets or private datasets to Perplexity.
Use a redaction pass before any file transfer.
Store sensitive AutoGPT outputs in a separate private directory.
Limit AutoGPT to non-sensitive test data.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning on uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and write via filesystem, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with no host execution, no filesystem write, and no git modification. The overlap is mostly read/analysis, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely.
conditions: IF Perplexity is manually used to edit files outside its documented surfaces, conflict risk would rise.
IF AutoGPT is pointed at the same directory as another writer, local file contention can occur.
mitigations: Assign AutoGPT and Perplexity separate working directories.
Avoid using Perplexity as a file editor.
Serialize any manual file updates through one operator.
Keep git operations out of the AutoGPT loop.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers and browsing context that AutoGPT could treat as authoritative if copied into its workflow. Because AutoGPT can act autonomously via shell and files, a mistaken Perplexity answer can cascade into incorrect downstream actions without verification.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted into AutoGPT without a verification step, errors can propagate.
IF AutoGPT is allowed to execute actions based on unreviewed search summaries, cascading mistakes are possible.
mitigations: Require a human fact-check before AutoGPT acts on Perplexity output.
Ask Perplexity for sources and verify them independently.
Constrain AutoGPT to dry-run mode for externally sourced tasks.
Separate research and execution roles.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for imported claims.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while AutoGPT is local/open-source with filesystem and shell access. No specific regulated data class is identified in either profile, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy mismatch rather than a documented residency or certification breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is uploaded into Perplexity, compliance review is required.
IF the operator uses AutoGPT on data subject to stricter retention or residency rules, policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Perplexity workflows.
Check vendor privacy terms before uploading documents.
Use synthetic data for testing.
Keep a record of what data classes each agent touches.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to approved environments.
